author: edu-critic-kestrel (independent education critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: B2/D3/C1: two of the eight Activity 2 scenarios ("final void ring() in class Bell, then class LoudBell extends Bell declares void ring()" and "final class Coin { } then class RareCoin extends Coin { }") depend on the extends keyword and on overriding in a subclass. The reading column never shows extends, no earlier page teaches it (grep found it nowhere before this topic; "subclass" appears undefined in access-modifiers), and the teaching itself says "Subclasses come in the next module". Yet the activity is only done when all eight go in on the first try, so a beginner can fail it on untaught syntax.
findings.recommendation: Add one worked line to the teaching showing "class RareCoin extends Coin" with a clause ("extends makes RareCoin a subclass, a class built on Coin"), or keep the method and class rules as stated facts and drop those two scenarios from the first-try requirement.

findings.claim: A1/G4: the card's decision is about toString, but the In interviews row ("what does final mean on a variable, a method and a class?") is about final, so it does not place this card's choice in an interview. The At work row ("A log line showing Card@1b6d3586 tells a teammate nothing") restates the teaching example rather than naming a situation in a junior's working week (a ticket, a review comment, a teammate debugging a failing build). "Use it when" also cites "logs or failed tests", and logging and tests are taught only in later modules.
findings.recommendation: Keep the card on toString and make both career rows about it, for example At work: "A teammate debugging an order bug asks you to make Order print its id and total in the logs instead of Order@...". In interviews: "You may be asked to write toString for a small class, as Activity 3 does." Gloss "logs" in a clause ("messages a program writes to record what it did"). Put the final interview probe in the topic's other material if wanted, not on this card.

findings.claim: B1: "hexadecimal number" (and "hex number" in Activity 4 feedback) is never explained, and hint 1 calls @Override "the annotation line" although the teaching never uses the word annotation. A career-changer does not know either word.
findings.recommendation: Add a clause: "a hexadecimal number (a code made of digits 0-9 and letters a-f)"; use "hex" nowhere or define it; say "the @Override line" in the hint.

findings.claim: D5: hint 2 for Activity 3 ("Build the text from three pieces joined with +: the rank field, the literal word between them with its spaces, and the suit field") spells out the finished return expression in prose, so it gives the answer rather than a reasoning step.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a reasoning step that points at the Point example's return line, for example "In Point, which parts of the return line are fields and which are fixed text? Map that to rank, suit and the word between them."

findings.claim: B4: the learner-facing title is "Reading: final and toString". "Reading:" is the syllabus row type, not part of the topic name, and this is an interactive page, so the prefix reads as authoring metadata (other topics in this module have plain titles).
findings.recommendation: Title the page "final and toString" in topic.json and the page; keep the kind in topic.json.

findings.claim: E1/B5: a wrong lane press gives "Not Compiles." or "Not Does not compile." because the verdict prefixes "Not" to the lane label. A beginner reads it as broken English at the moment they are confused.
findings.recommendation: Phrase the wrong-lane verdict as "Not this lane: <lane label>" or "Not 'Compiles'", in the engine wording shared across pages.

findings.claim: A4: Activity 2 practises the probe in the In interviews row exactly ("what does final mean on a variable, a method and a class?"), and the page does not say so (and the row sits on the toString card, see C2-EDU-FIN-02).
findings.recommendation: When the career rows are reworked, say which activity practises the probe.

findings.claim: Other real problem (E1/F5): the practice editor does not check statements inside method or constructor bodies. Exercised at 570 px: Card.java with "this.suit = suit" (missing ";") inside the constructor, or "return rank + " of " + suit" without ";", is accepted. The Problems tab says "No problems found in the parts this editor reads" and feedback says "All 5 checks pass", while other syntax errors on the same page are reported as "the compiler would reject this code". A beginner reads the pass as "this compiles" and learns that the missing semicolon or bracket is fine. Overlaps the SME fidelity review.
findings.recommendation: Either have the parser require a terminating ";" and balanced parentheses on body statements, reporting them through the existing "Not checked ... does not count as a try" path, or state beside Check code that statement punctuation inside methods is not checked, so the pass is not read as "compiles".

location.selector: #activity-3 #fb-3 (inline engine: second checked try, verdict set)

findings.claim: E3 (practice-feedback-policy 1.1): a near-miss is only treated as one on the first checked try ("Almost: ..."). On the second (last) checked try the same one-detail miss leads with the failure verdict "Not this time: N-1 of N checks pass after your second checked try" (observed for a toString without @Override), and the activity is closed for credit. The policy says a near-miss never gets a failure verdict.
findings.recommendation: When exactly one check fails on the last checked try, lead with the near-miss verdict ("Almost: ...") and the specific nudge, in pep-verdict--near styling, then state that the result is recorded and practice can continue.

findings.claim: B5/G1: the completion summary names activities by internal labels ("What final forbids", "Override toString", "Final check") that match none of the lesson-path row titles the learner has seen ("Sort what final forbids", "Make a card print readably", "Predict what gets logged"). A learner told "Final check: answered, not yet correct" has to guess which activity that is.
findings.recommendation: Make each PEP_PAGE label equal to its lesson-path row title, or have the completion summary read the row title.

findings.claim: B2/GIFT: the "String toString()" distractor's feedback relies on "narrows the inherited access, which the compiler rejects", a rule the page states only inside a check message, and the o1 items lean on subclass behaviour the page defers to the next module. Low because the page does teach the public String toString() shape.
findings.recommendation: Gloss the rule in the feedback ("toString is public in Object, so an override must stay public").

location.selector: h2 "Cheat sheet" and h2 "Static interaction alternatives"

findings.claim: Other real problem (companion): the Markdown companion files every hint, the optional anecdote or challenge text under the "Cheat sheet" heading, repeats the summary text ("Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 for Activity 3"), titles the static alternatives with engine type names ("predict", "drag", "explore", "mcq"; the lane activity is not dragged), and omits the On the job card with its At work and In interviews rows. The same generator output appears on all 255 topics, so this is a tooling defect rather than this page's authoring.
findings.recommendation: Raise a tooling-branch fix: give hints, anecdote and challenge their own headings, use activity titles instead of interaction types, de-duplicate summary text and carry the On the job card. No page-level change needed in this module branch.
